name: Sungtachi Kodi
subtitle: everyday prawn and drumstick curry in a thin red coconut masala

ingredients.note: adds the sweetness that makes this curry

prepNotes: Toss the prawns with 1/4 tsp turmeric and a pinch of salt and leave 15 minutes, then rinse and drain well.
Rinse the kokum petals and soak them in 3 tbsp warm water while you grind the masala.
Peel the drumsticks with a knife, leaving the tender inner rib — the tough outer skin never softens.

steps.text: Grind the coconut, Kashmiri chillies, coriander powder, cumin, turmeric and garlic with 250ml warm water to a completely smooth paste.
steps.tip: Blend for a full four minutes. A gritty masala is the commonest fault in a home coconut curry.

steps.text: Boil the drumstick pieces in 250ml salted water for 8 minutes, until a fingernail marks the flesh easily. Keep the water.
Heat the coconut oil in a wide pan and soften the onion 5 minutes until translucent.
Pour in the ground masala along with the drumstick and its cooking water, add the green chillies and salt, and bring to a simmer.
Simmer 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until the raw smell of the coconut has gone and the curry looks glossy rather than chalky.
steps.tip: Do not let it reach a rolling boil once the coconut is in — it will split.

steps.text: Add the kokum with its soaking water and simmer 2 minutes.
Slide in the prawns and cook 3-4 minutes only, until they curl and turn opaque.
steps.tip: Prawns go from done to rubbery in about a minute. Pull the pan as soon as they curve into a C.

steps.text: Take off the heat, check the salt and sourness, and rest 5 minutes before serving with rice.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated, though the prawns firm up. Reheat over low heat just to steaming. Do not freeze.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
